job.title: English Language Teacher
job.description:
English Language Teacher | Years 7–12 | Independent School

Melbourne's Outer West | January 2027 | $87,000–$132,000 + Super

  • Teach English Language in a well-established independent school with strong academic standards and clear classroom expectations.
  • Work with culturally and linguistically diverse students in a structured, academically focused environment.
  • Access ongoing professional development, established teaching resources and class sizes of approximately 20–25 students.

About the School

HARKE Recruitment has partnered with a leading co-educational, non-denominational independent school in Melbourne's outer west. The school has a strong reputation for academic achievement, structured learning and high expectations. The school prioritises explicit instruction, strong subject knowledge and consistent classroom practices. Teachers benefit from an established leadership team, ongoing professional development and a collaborative environment where academic growth and student accountability are central to teaching and learning.

About the Position

HARKE is seeking an English Language Teacher for Years 7–10, with the ability to offer VCE highly desirable. This position will commence in Term 1 (January) 2027 on a 12-month contract with view to go ongoing.

This position is particularly suited to teachers with experience or academic expertise in VCE English Language, linguistics or language analysis.

Unlike mainstream English, which places significant emphasis on literature and textual interpretation, English Language explores how language is constructed, used and influenced by social and cultural contexts.

The school is seeking a teacher who can confidently introduce linguistic concepts to junior and middle secondary students, building their understanding of language structures, metalanguage, language variation and the relationship between language and identity.

With a culturally diverse student population and strong academic expectations, this is an opportunity to teach language beyond traditional text study while developing students' analytical and communication skills.

Skills and Responsibilities

  • Deliver structured, engaging English Language lessons across Years 7–10, using explicit instruction and clear learning intentions.
  • Teach linguistic concepts including syntax, semantics, morphology, language variation and sociolinguistics through practical, age-appropriate examples.
  • Develop students' ability to analyse spoken and written language, including how language reflects culture, identity and social context.
  • Maintain high expectations for classroom behaviour, student progress and academic achievement, providing regular assessment and feedback.
  • Collaborate with the English faculty to strengthen curriculum planning, consistent teaching practices and student pathways towards VCE English Language.

About You

The school is seeking a teacher with strong subject knowledge, clear instructional practices and an interest in how language works, rather than a solely literature-focused approach to English.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Knowledge of VCE English Language, linguistic frameworks and relevant metalanguage.
  • The ability to explain language structures and linguistic concepts clearly to Years 7–10 students.
  • Confidence using explicit teaching, assessment data and structured classroom routines to support student achievement.
  • An understanding of language diversity and the ability to engage students from varied linguistic and cultural backgrounds.
  • Strong communication, classroom management and collaboration skills.

Graduate teachers with relevant tertiary studies in linguistics or English Language are encouraged to apply. Previous experience teaching VCE English Language will be highly regarded.

Requirements

  • Registration with, or eligibility for registration with, the Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT).
  • Full Australian working rights. Visa sponsorship is not available.
  • Two professional referees and completion of HARKE Recruitment's safeguarding and onboarding requirements.

How to Apply

To be considered, please submit your CV and a short cover letter (maximum one page) via SEEK addressing the following:

  1. English Language expertise: Outline your experience or studies in English Language, linguistics or VCE English Language. Include specific areas of expertise, such as metalanguage, language structures, sociolinguistics or language variation.
  2. Teaching approach: Provide an example of how you would use explicit instruction to introduce a linguistic concept to Years 7–10 students and assess their understanding.
  3. School suitability: Explain how you establish high academic expectations, maintain a structured classroom and support students from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Applications should include relevant examples from classroom teaching, professional placements or tertiary studies.

HARKE has partnered with a growing Christian school in the outer North West suburbs of Melbourne that is committed to nurturing students academically, spiritually and personally. With approximately 200 students, the school offers a close-knit community where strong relationships between staff, students and families are highly valued.

Educators benefit from a supportive leadership team, a collaborative culture, additional non-teaching days throughout the year, and an earlier finish to the school year. The school is continuing to invest in its specialist programs and provides opportunities for teachers to contribute to the future direction of learning across the College.

About the Position

This ongoing part-time position involves teaching Music across Prep to Year 6 over three days per week, commencing Term 1, 2027. The successful candidate will deliver an engaging primary Music program focused on developing student confidence, creativity, participation and musical skills. The role also provides an opportunity to contribute to the continued development of the school's Music program, including potential expansion of instrumental offerings such as guitar and keyboard.

Skills and Responsibilities

  • Deliver engaging Music lessons for students across Prep to Year 6.
  • Foster student creativity, confidence and participation through classroom and performance-based learning.
  • Maintain a safe and supportive learning environment aligned with safeguarding requirements.
  • Collaborate with colleagues to support whole-school activities, performances and student learning outcomes.
  • Contribute to the continued development of the school's Music program and instrumental offerings.

Requirements

  • Registration: Candidates must hold or be eligible to obtain Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) registration. Permission to Teach candidates will also be considered.
  • Faith Alignment: Applicants must demonstrate an active Christian faith, provide a pastoral reference, and align with the school's Protestant Christian ethos.
  • Work Rights: Full Australian working rights are essential for this role.
  • Safeguarding: Applicants must provide two current referees and complete HARKE’s onboarding process to meet safeguarding requirements.
